288.subject: Botany
288.text: Bacteria, fungi, lower plants survive in adverse conditions by
288.sol: Bacteria, fungi and lower plants survive in adverse conditions through formation of thick walled spores. Algae form resting spore or akinetes which are thick walled spores and store food material. In fungi, thick walled perennating spores called chlamydospores are formed. Bacteria form endospores which is probably the most resistant living thing known. They may remain alive in boiling water for more than 2 hours.

1843.text: Which of the following physical quantities do not have same dimensions?
1843.sol:
Pressure and stress both have the dimensions of force/area. Strain and angle are both dimensionsless. Energy and work have the same dimensions force \(\times\) distance.
Tension and surface tension refer to two different physical quantities and their dimensions are different. Tension is a force and surface tension is force per unit length.

5828.text: The pressure exerted by a mixture of $3. 2g$ of methane and $4. 4g$ of ${CO}_{2}$ contained in a $9{dm}^{3}$ flask at $27 ° C$ is
5828.sol:
The pressure exerted by methane is $P = \dfrac{nRT}{V}$

$= \dfrac{0. 2 \times 8. 314 \times 300}{9 \times {10}^{- 3}} = 5. 54 \times {10}^{4}Pa$

The pressure exerted by ${CO}_{2}$ is $P^{'} = \dfrac{n ' RT}{V}$

$= \dfrac{0. 1 \times 8. 314 \times 300}{9 \times {10}^{- 3}} = 2. 77 \times {10}^{4}Pa$

The total pressure is $P + P^{'}$.

$= \left(5. 54 \times {10}^{4}Pa\right) + \left(2. 77 \times {10}^{4}Pa\right) = 8. 31 \times {10}^{4}Pa$

6959.subject: Mathematics
6959.text: Given two fixed points $A ( - 2, 1 )$ and $B (3,0)$, find the locus of a point $P$ which moves such that the angle $∠ APB$ is always a right angle.
6959.sol:
Let, the coordinates& of point& $P \left(h, k\right)

Given, points A \left(-2, 1\right) and& $B $\left(3, 0\right)$,

So, the slope of $AP$ is (Say ${m}_{1}$) $\dfrac{k - 1}{h + 2},

and,$ the slope ofBP$ is (Say& {m}_{2})\dfrac{k - 0}{h - 3} = \dfrac{k}{h - 3}

As, $∠ APB = 90 °$

Hence, ${m}_{1}{m}_{2} = - 1$

\dfrac{k - 1}{h + 2}$ \times $\dfrac{k}{h - 3} =-1 ⇒ \dfrac{k^{2} - k}{h^{2} + 2h - 3h - 6} = -1 ⇒ \dfrac{k^{2} - k}{h^{2} - h - 6} = -1$

$k^{2} - k = - \left(h^{2} - h - 6\right) ⇒ k^{2} + h^{2} - k - h - 6 = 0$

So, replace $\left( h, k\right)$ \to $\left(x, y\right)$, in order to obtain the locus.

Hence, the locus of point& $P$ is& $x^{2} + y^{2} - x - y - 6 = 0$

10430.text: A student is allowed to choose atmost \(n\) books from a collection of \(2 n+1\) books. If the total number of ways in which he can select atleast one book is 255 , then the value of \(n\) is
10430.sol:
According to given information,
\begin{aligned}& { }^{2 n+1} C_1+{ }^{2 n+1} C_2+{ }^{2 n+1} C_3+\ldots \ldots+{ }^{2 n+1} C_n=x $\text{ Let}$\\
& \because^{2 n+1} C_0+{ }^{2 n+1} C_1+{ }^{2 n+1} C_2+\ldots+{ }^{2 n+1} C_n+\ldots \\
& +\binom{2 n+1}{2 n+1}=2^{2 n+1} \\
& \Rightarrow 2 x+{ }^{2 n+1} C_0+\binom{2 n+1}{2 n+1}=2^{2 n+1} \\
& ${\left[\because{ }^ n C_{n-r}={ }^n C_r\right]}$\\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 x+1+1=2^{2 n+1} \\
& ${\left[\because{ }^ n C_0={ }^n C_n=1\right]}$\\
& \Rightarrow \quad x=2^{2 n}-1=255 \quad $\text{(given)}$\\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2^{2 n}=256=2^8 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad n=4 \\
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (1) is correct.

13352.text: Let \(\mathbf{m}\) be a vector of magnitude \(\sqrt{3}\) and perpendicular to the vectors \(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}\) and \(\hat{\mathbf{j}}-\hat{\mathbf{k}}\). Let \(\mathbf{n}\) be another vector of magnitude \(2 \sqrt{6}\) and perpendicular to the vectors \(2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}\) and \(\hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}\). The area (in sq. units) of the triangle formed with \(\mathbf{m}\) and \(\mathbf{n}\) as sides is
13352.sol:
Given,
\(\mathbf{m}=\sqrt{3} \times \text{ unit vectors of }[(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}) \times(\hat{\mathbf{j}}-\hat{\mathbf{k}})]\)
\(\begin{aligned}
\because(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}) \times(\hat{\mathbf{j}}-\hat{\mathbf{k}}) & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
\hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\
1 & 1 & 0 \\
0 & 1 & -1
\end{array}\right] \\
& =\hat{\mathbf{i}}(-1-0)-\hat{\mathbf{j}}(-1-0)+\hat{\mathbf{k}}(\mathbf{l}) \\
& =-\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}} \\
\therefore \quad \mathbf{m} & =\sqrt{3} \times \frac{-\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}}{\sqrt{1+1+1}} \\
& =\sqrt{3} \times \frac{-\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}}{\sqrt{3}}=-\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}
\end{aligned}\) and \(\mathbf{n}=2 \sqrt{6} \times\) unit vectors of \([(2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}) \times(\hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}})]\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& \therefore(2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}) \times(\hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}) \\
&=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
\hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\
2 & -1 & 0 \\
0 & 1 & 2
\end{array}\right] \\
&=\hat{\mathbf{i}}(-2-0)-\hat{\mathbf{j}}(4-0)+\hat{\mathbf{k}}(2+0)=-2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-4 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\
& \mathbf{n}=2 \sqrt{6} \times \frac{-2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-4 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}}{\sqrt{4+16+4}}=2 \sqrt{6} \times \frac{-2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-4 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}}{2 \sqrt{6}}
\end{aligned}\)
\(=-2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-4 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}\)
Now, required area
\(\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{m} \times \mathbf{n})=\frac{1}{2}|(-\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}) \times(-2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-4 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}})| \\
& =\frac{1}{2}\left|$\begin{array}{ccc}
\hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \hat{\mathbf{k}} \\
-1 & 1 & 1 \\
-2 & -4 & 2
\end{array}$\right| \\
& =\frac{1}{2} \times \mid \hat{\mathbf{i}}(2+4)-\hat{\mathbf{j}}(-2+2)+\hat{\mathbf{k}}(4+2|| \\
& =\frac{1}{2} \times|6 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+6 \hat{\mathbf{k}}|=\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{6^2+6^2}=\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times \sqrt{2}=3 \sqrt{2}
\end{aligned}\)

Equation of projectile motion is given by

General equation of projectile motion,

$\tan \theta=12\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}=12\sin \theta=12 \cos \theta$
Multiplying on both side by $(u)u \sin \theta=12(u \cos \theta)=12 \times 3$

16769.text:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding \(p-V\) graph?
1. Slope of \(p-V\) graph in an isothermal process is \(-\frac{p}{V}\).
2. Slope of \(p-V\) graph in an adiabatic process is \(-\frac{p}{V}\).
3. Slope of \(p-V\) graph in an isochoric process is \(-\frac{\gamma p}{V}\).
4. Slope of \(p-V\) graph in an isobaric process is zero.
16769.sol:
(i) and (iv) options are correct. (i) Slope of \(p-V\) graph in an isothermal process is \(-\frac{p}{V}\) this is correct.
For isothermal process, slope of \(p-V^{\prime}\) curve \(\frac{d p}{d V}=-\frac{p}{V}\) (ii) Slope of \(p-V\) group in an adiabatic process is \(-\frac{p}{V}\), which is wrong.
Because slope of \(p-V\) graph in an adiabatic process is \(-\frac{\gamma p}{V}\). (iii) Slope of \(p\) - \(V\) graph in an isochoric process is \(-\frac{\gamma p}{V}\) this option is wrong. Because slope of \(p-V\) graph for isochoric process is \(\frac{d p}{-\frac{d V}{V}}-\frac{d V}{V}=\frac{d p}{0}=\infty\)
(d) Slope of \(p-V\) graph in an isobaric process is zero. This option is correct.
\(p-V\) curve is a straight line parallel to volume axis, slope of \(p\) - \(V\) curve for an isobaric process \(\frac{d p}{d V}=0.\)

19990.subject: Chemistry
19990.text:
Arrange the complex ions in the increasing order of their magnetic moments
A. $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$
B. $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$
C. $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-}$
D. $\left[\mathrm{FeF}_6\right]^{3-}$
19990.sol:
The magnetic moment is calculated using the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ B.M., where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

A. In $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6\right]^{2+}$, Fe is in $+2$ oxidation state ($3d^6$). $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ is a weak field ligand, so electrons remain unpaired: $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 4$. $\mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90$ B.M.

B. In $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$, Fe is in $+2$ oxidation state ($3d^6$). $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ is a strong field ligand, causing pairing: $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 0$. $\mu = 0$ B.M.

C. In $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-}$, Fe is in $+3$ oxidation state ($3d^5$). $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ is a strong field ligand, causing pairing: $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 1$. $\mu = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73$ B.M.

D. In $\left[\mathrm{FeF}_6\right]^{3-}$, Fe is in $+3$ oxidation state ($3d^5$). $\mathrm{F}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so electrons remain unpaired: $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 5$. $\mu = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92$ B.M.

Comparing the magnetic moments: $0 \lt 1.73 \lt 4.90 \lt 5.92$, which corresponds to $\mathrm{B} \lt \mathrm{C} \lt \mathrm{A} \lt \mathrm{D}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{B} \lt \mathrm{C} \lt \mathrm{A} \lt \mathrm{D}$

20051.subject: Chemistry
20051.text:
Pick out the correct option
Assertion(A): Mercury is not considered as a transition element
Reason (R): Mercury is a liquid
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
20051.sol:
Assertion (A) is true because transition elements are defined as elements having incompletely filled d-orbitals in their ground state or in any of their common oxidation states. Mercury (Hg) has a completely filled d-orbital (5d^{10}$) in its ground state as well as in its common oxidation states. Hence, it is not considered a transition element.

Reason (R) is true because mercury is indeed a liquid at room temperature.

However, the physical state (being a liquid) is not the reason for mercury not being classified as a transition element. The correct reason is its electronic configuration.

Therefore, both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

Answer: Both A and R are true, R is not the correct explanation of A$

20631.subject: Chemistry
20631.text: An aqueous solution which contains $42 \%$ by weight ( $\mathrm{w} / \mathrm{W}$ ) of a volatile liquid " A " of molar mass of $140 \mathrm{ g} / \mathrm{mol}$, has a vapour pressure of 2141.4 mm of Hg at $37^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$. What is the vapour pressure of the pure liquid "A"? Vapour pressure of water at $37^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ is 2019.1 mm .
20631.sol:
Let the total mass of the solution be $100 \text{ g}$.

Mass of solute A = $42 \text{ g}$.
Mass of solvent (water) = $100 - 42 = 58 \text{ g}$.

Molar mass of A ($M_A$) = $140 \text{ g/mol}$.
Molar mass of water ($M_W$) = $18 \text{ g/mol}$.

Number of moles of A ($n_A$) = $\dfrac{42}{140} = 0.3 \text{ mol}$.
Number of moles of water ($n_W$) = $\dfrac{58}{18} = 3.222 \text{ mol}$.

Mole fraction of A ($x_A$) = $\dfrac{n_A}{n_A + n_W} = \dfrac{0.3}{0.3 + 3.222} = \dfrac{0.3}{3.522} \approx 0.08518$.
Mole fraction of water ($x_W$) = $1 - x_A = 1 - 0.08518 = 0.91482$.

According to Raoult's Law for a solution of two volatile liquids:
$P_{total} = P_A^{0} x_A + P_W^{0} x_W$

Given $P_{total} = 2141.4 \text{ mm Hg}$ and $P_W^{0} = 2019.1 \text{ mm Hg}$:
$2141.4 = P_A^{0} (0.08518) + 2019.1 (0.91482)$

$2141.4 = P_A^{0} (0.08518) + 1847.10$

$P_A^{0} (0.08518) = 2141.4 - 1847.10 = 294.3$

$P_A^{0} = \dfrac{294.3}{0.08518} \approx 3455.03 \text{ mm Hg}$..

Answer: 3455.0 nm

20854.subject: Chemistry
20854.text: Given that the standard enthalpy of combustion of $\mathrm{C}_{(\mathrm{S})}$ and $\mathrm{CS}_2(\mathrm{l})$ are -393.3 and $-1108.76 \mathrm{ kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$ respectively and the standard enthalpy of formation of $\mathrm{CS}_2$ is $128.02 \mathrm{ kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$. What is $\Delta H_f^0$ of $\mathrm{SO}_2$ ?
20854.sol:
The combustion reactions are given as follows:

1. $\mathrm{C}_{(\mathrm{s})} + \mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_{2(\mathrm{g})}$, $\Delta H_1 = -393.3 \text{ kJ/mol}$

2. $\mathrm{CS}_{2(\mathrm{l})} + 3\mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + 2\mathrm{SO}_{2(\mathrm{g})}$, $\Delta H_2 = -1108.76 \text{ kJ/mol}$

The enthalpy of formation of $\mathrm{CS}_{2(\mathrm{l})}$ is given by the reaction:

3. $\mathrm{C}_{(\mathrm{s})} + 2\mathrm{S}_{(\mathrm{s})} \rightarrow \mathrm{CS}_{2(\mathrm{l})}$, $\Delta H_f^0(\mathrm{CS}_2) = 128.02 \text{ kJ/mol}$

The enthalpy of combustion of $\mathrm{CS}_{2(\mathrm{l})}$ can be expressed in terms of enthalpies of formation:

$\Delta H_2 = [\Delta H_f^0(\mathrm{CO}_2) + 2\Delta H_f^0(\mathrm{SO}_2)] - [\Delta H_f^0(\mathrm{CS}_2) + 3\Delta H_f^0(\mathrm{O}_2)]$

Since $\Delta H_f^0(\mathrm{CO}_2) = \Delta H_1 = -393.3 \text{ kJ/mol}$ and $\Delta H_f^0(\mathrm{O}_2) = 0$, we substitute the values:

$-1108.76 = [-393.3 + 2\Delta H_f^0(\mathrm{SO}_2)] - [128.02 + 0]$

$-1108.76 = -393.3 + 2\Delta H_f^0(\mathrm{SO}_2) - 128.02$

$-1108.76 = -521.32 + 2\Delta H_f^0(\mathrm{SO}_2)$

$2\Delta H_f^0(\mathrm{SO}_2) = -1108.76 + 521.32 = -587.44$

$\Delta H_f^0(\mathrm{SO}_2) = -293.72 \text{ kJ/mol}$

Answer: $-293.72 \mathrm{ kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$

21875.subject: Mathematics
21875.text: An engineering team is testing a new prototype drone. The drone has constant success rate of $\dfrac{2}{7} for every autonomous landing attempt. Two engineers, Sarah and Swarna, take turns initiating the landing sequence, with Swarna going first. If they continue the process until a landing is successful, what is the probability that Sarah is the one who initiates the successful landing?$
21875.sol:
Let $p$ be the probability of a successful landing and $q$ be the probability of a failed landing.

$p = \dfrac{2}{7}$

$q = 1 - \dfrac{2}{7} = \dfrac{5}{7}$

Swarna attempts first, followed by Sarah. Sarah initiates the successful landing if the first success occurs on the 2nd, 4th, 6th, $\dots$ attempt.

The probability of this happening is given by the sum of the probabilities of these mutually exclusive events:

$P(\text{Sarah}) = qp + q^3p + q^5p + \dots$

This is an infinite geometric progression with first term $a = qp$ and common ratio $r = q^2$.

$P(\text{Sarah}) = \dfrac{qp}{1 - q^2}$

Substituting the values of $p$ and $q$:

$P(\text{Sarah}) = \dfrac{\dfrac{5}{7} \times \dfrac{2}{7}}{1 - \left(\dfrac{5}{7}\right)^2}$

$P(\text{Sarah}) = \dfrac{\dfrac{10}{49}}{1 - \dfrac{25}{49}}$

$P(\text{Sarah}) = \dfrac{\dfrac{10}{49}}{\dfrac{24}{49}}$

$P(\text{Sarah}) = \dfrac{10}{24} = \dfrac{5}{12}$

Answer: $\dfrac{5}{12}$

21884.subject: Mathematics
21884.text: A bag contains $(n+1)$ coins. It is known that one of these coins has a head on both sides, whereas the other coins are fair. One of these coins is selected at random and tossed. If the probability that the toss results in heads is $\dfrac{7}{12}$, then the value of $n$ is
21884.sol:
Let $E$ be the event that the selected coin shows heads. Let $C_1$ be the event that the two-headed coin is selected, and $C_2$ be the event that a fair coin is selected.

The probability of selecting the two-headed coin is $P(C_1) = \dfrac{1}{n+1}$.

The probability of selecting a fair coin is $P(C_2) = \dfrac{n}{n+1}$.

The probability of getting heads given the two-headed coin is $P(E|C_1) = 1$.

The probability of getting heads given a fair coin is $P(E|C_2) = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Using the law of total probability, $P(E) = P(E|C_1)P(C_1) + P(E|C_2)P(C_2)$.

Substituting the known values, $\dfrac{7}{12} = (1) \left(\dfrac{1}{n+1}\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(\dfrac{n}{n+1}\right).

Multiplying by $2(n+1)$, we get \dfrac{7}{12} \times$2(n+1) = 2 + n$.

\dfrac{7(n+1)}{6} =$n + 2$.

$7n + 7 = 6n + 12$.

$n = 5$.

Answer: 5$

26105.subject: Physics
26105.text: Heater of an electric kettle is made of a wire of length L and diameter d. It takes 4 minutes to raise the temperature of 0.5 kg water by 40 K. This heater is replaced by a new heater having two wires of the same material, each of length L and diameter 2d. The way these wires are connected is given in the options. How much time in minutes will it take to raise the temperature of the same amount of water by 40K?
26105.sol:
Joules law,

\(\mathrm{H}=\mathrm{I}^{2} \mathrm{Rt}=\frac{\mathrm{V}^{2} \mathrm{t}}{\mathrm{R}}\)

Also,

\(\mathrm{R}=\rho \frac{1}{\mathrm{ A}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{R} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{ A}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{R} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{r}^{2}}\)

\(\therefore R^{\prime}=\frac{R}{4}\)

parallel \(\Rightarrow \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{p}}=\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{R} / 4}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{R} / 4}\right)^{-1}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{8}\)

\(\text{ series } \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{s}}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{4}+\frac{\mathrm{R}}{4}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{2}\)

\(\therefore \frac{\mathrm{V}^{2} 4}{\mathrm{R}}=\frac{\mathrm{V}^{2} \mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{p}}}=\frac{\mathrm{V}^{2} \mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{s}}}{\mathrm{R}_\mathrm{s}}\)

\(\Rightarrow \mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{p}}=0.5 \mathrm{ min}, \mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{s}}=2 \mathrm{ min}\)

26344.subject: Physics
26344.text: Consider the motion of a positive point charge in a region where there are simultaneous uniform electric and magnetic fields $\vec{E}=E_{0} \hat{j}$ and $\vec{B}=B_{0} \hat{j}$. At time $t=0$, this charge has velocity $\vec{v}$ in the in the $x$-y plane, making an angle $\theta$ with the $x$-axis. Which of the following option(s) is (are) correct for time $t>0$ ?
options: If $\theta=0^{\circ}$, the charge moves in a circular path in the $x$ - plane.
If $\theta=0^{\circ}$, the charge undergoes helical motion with constant pitch along the $y$-axis.
If $\theta=10^{\circ}$, the charge undergoes helical motion with its pitch increasing with time, along the $y$-axis.
If $\theta=90^{\circ}$, the charge undergoes linear but accelerated motion along the $y$-axis.
26344.sol: If $\theta=0^{\circ}$, the charged particle is projected along $x$-axis, due to magnetic field, $\vec{B}$ the charged particle will tend to move in a circular path in $y-z$ plane but due to force of electric field $\vec{E}$, the particle will move in a helical path with increasing pitch. Hence options (A) and (B) are wrong. If $\theta=10^{\circ}$, we can resolve velocity into two rectangular components. One along $x$-axis $\left(v \cos 10^{\circ}\right)$ and one along $y$-axis $\left(v \sin 10^{\circ}\right)$. Due to $v \cos 10^{\circ}$, the particle will move in circular path and due to $v \sin 10^{\circ}$ plus the force due to electric field, the particle will undergo helical motion with its pitch increasing. If $\theta=90^{\circ}$, the charge is moving along the magnetic field. Therefore the force due to magnetic field is zero. But the force due to electric field will accelerate the particle along $y$-axis.

26716.text: Sometimes it is convenient to construct a system of units so that all quantities can be expressed in terms of only one physical quantity. In one such system, dimensions of different quantities are given in terms of a quantity $X$ as follows: $\left[position\right] = \left[{X}^{\alpha}\right]; \left[speed\right] = \left[{X}^{\beta}\right]; \left[acceleration\right] = \left[{X}^{p}\right];\left[linearmomentum\right]$ = $\left[{X}^{q}\right]$; $\left[force\right]$ = $\left[{X}^{r}\right]$. Then
26716.sol:
$\left[\dfrac{momentum}{Force}\right] = {X}^{p - r}$

$⇒ \left[\dfrac{mv}{ma}\right] = {X}^{p - r}$

$⇒ \left[\dfrac{v}{a}\right] = {X}^{p - r}$

but given that $\dfrac{v}{a} = {X}^{\beta - p}$

So,

$p - r = \beta - p ⇒ 2p = \beta + r . . . \left(1\right)$

$\left[\dfrac{spee{d}^{2}}{acceleration}\right] = \left[position\right] ⇒ \dfrac{{X}^{2\beta}}{{X}^{p}} = {X}^{\alpha} ⇒ 2\beta - p = \alpha ⇒ p + \alpha = 2\beta . . . \left(2\right)$

and

$\left[\dfrac{force}{linearmomentum}\right] = \left[\dfrac{acceleration}{speed}\right] ⇒ \left[\dfrac{{X}^{r}}{{X}^{q}}\right] = \left[\dfrac{{X}^{p}}{{X}^{\beta}}\right] ⇒ r - q = p - \beta ⇒ p + q - r = \beta . . . \left(3\right)$

27785.text:
The number of non-polar molecules from the following is
$HF, {H}_{2}O, {SO}_{2}, {H}_{2}, {CO}_{2}, {CH}_{4}, {NH}_{3}, HCl, {CHCl}_{3}, {BF}_{3}$
27785.sol:
The molecules which have perfect geometry and no lone pairs are zero dipole moment molecules. Those molecules termed as non-polar molecules. Amongst the given compounds, ${CH}_{4}, {CO}_{2}, {H}_{2}, {BF}_{3}$ are non polar molecules.

${H}_{2}O$ has two lone pairs and two bond pairs. ${SO}_{2}$ has two sigma bond pairs and one lone pair. ${CHCl}_{3}$ has net dipole moment because the bond moments do not cancel with each other. ${NH}_{3}$ have one lone pair and three bond pairs. In $HF$ bond moment is the dipole moment. Hence, all these molecules have some net dipole moment.

The non-polar molecules are ${CO}_{2}, {H}_{2}, {CH}_{4}$ and ${BF}_{3}$

34114.text: Let $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}(x-1) \sin\left(\frac{1}{x-1}\right), & \text{ if } x \neq 1 \\ 0, & \text{ if } x=1\end{array}\right.$. Then which one of the following is true?

$f$ is differentiable at $x=0$ and at $x=1$

34191.sol:
Let, $I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{{x}^{2}sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x} d x$

Now using the property ${∫}_{0}^{2a}f\left(x\right) d x = {∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(x\right) d x + {∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(2a - x\right) d x$ we get,

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}\left({x}^{2} - {\left(\pi - x\right)}^{2}\right) d x$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}\left(2\pi x - {\pi}^{2}\right) d x$

$⇒ I = 2\pi\mathop{\mathop{{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{x \cdot sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x} d x}_{⏟}}_{{I}_{1}} - {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x} d x$

Now, solving ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{x \cdot sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}dx . . . . \left(1\right)$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right) \cdot sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}dx . . . . \left(2\right)$

Adding both equations we get,

$⇒ 2{I}_{1} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}dx$

Now, putting the value in $I$ we get,

$⇒ I = 2\pi \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{4}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{x \cdot sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}dx - {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x} d x$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x} d x$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sinxcosx}{1 - 2\sin^{2}x\cos^{2}x} d x$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}sin2x}{1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{2}2x} d x$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sin2x}{2 - \sin^{2}2x} d x$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{sin2x}{1 + \cos^{2}2x} d x$

Now, let $cos2x = t ⇒ - 2sin2xdx = dt$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{2}{∫}_{1}^{- 1}\dfrac{- \dfrac{1}{2}}{1 + {t}^{2}} d t$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{4}{∫}_{- 1}^{1}\dfrac{1}{1 + {t}^{2}} d t$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{4} \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{2} = - \dfrac{{\pi}^{3}}{8}$

Hence, $\dfrac{120}{{\pi}^{3}}\left|{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{{x}^{2}sinxcosx}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x} d x\right| = \dfrac{120}{{\pi}^{3}} \times \dfrac{{\pi}^{3}}{8} = 15$

34633.subject: Mathematics
34633.text: Let $y = y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $(x^2 - x\sqrt{x^2 - 1})dy + (y(x - \sqrt{x^2 - 1}) - x)dx = 0$, $x \geq 1$. If $y(1) = 1$, then the greatest integer less than $y(\sqrt{5})$ is _______.
34633.sol:
The given differential equation is:

$(x^2 - x\sqrt{x^2 - 1})dy + (y(x - \sqrt{x^2 - 1}) - x)dx = 0$

Dividing the entire equation by $dx$ and rearranging, we get:

$x(x - \sqrt{x^2 - 1}) \dfrac{dy}{dx} + y(x - \sqrt{x^2 - 1}) = x$

Dividing by $x(x - \sqrt{x^2 - 1})$, we obtain a linear differential equation:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{1}{x}y = \dfrac{1}{x - \sqrt{x^2 - 1}}$

The integrating factor (I.F.) is:

$\text{I.F.} = e^{\int \dfrac{1}{x} dx} = e^{\ln x} = x$

Multiplying the differential equation by the integrating factor $x$, we get:

$x \dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = \dfrac{x}{x - \sqrt{x^2 - 1}}$

$\dfrac{d}{dx}(xy) = \dfrac{x(x + \sqrt{x^2 - 1})}{(x - \sqrt{x^2 - 1})(x + \sqrt{x^2 - 1})}$

$\dfrac{d}{dx}(xy) = \dfrac{x^2 + x\sqrt{x^2 - 1}}{x^2 - (x^2 - 1)}$

$\dfrac{d}{dx}(xy) = x^2 + x\sqrt{x^2 - 1}$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$:

$\int d(xy) = \int (x^2 + x\sqrt{x^2 - 1}) dx$

$xy = \dfrac{x^3}{3} + \dfrac{(x^2 - 1)^{3/2}}{3} + C$

Given $y(1) = 1$, we substitute $x = 1$ and $y = 1$:

$1(1) = \dfrac{1^3}{3} + 0 + C \Rightarrow C = 1 - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

So, the particular solution is:

$xy = \dfrac{x^3}{3} + \dfrac{(x^2 - 1)^{3/2}}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3}$

To find $y(\sqrt{5})$, we substitute $x = \sqrt{5}$:

$\sqrt{5} y(\sqrt{5}) = \dfrac{(\sqrt{5})^3}{3} + \dfrac{(5 - 1)^{3/2}}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3}$

$\sqrt{5} y(\sqrt{5}) = \dfrac{5\sqrt{5}}{3} + \dfrac{4^{3/2}}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3}$

$\sqrt{5} y(\sqrt{5}) = \dfrac{5\sqrt{5}}{3} + \dfrac{8}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{5\sqrt{5} + 10}{3}$

$y(\sqrt{5}) = \dfrac{5}{3} + \dfrac{10}{3\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{5 + 2\sqrt{5}}{3}$

Since $\sqrt{5} \approx 2.236$, we have $2\sqrt{5} \approx 4.472$.

$y(\sqrt{5}) \approx \dfrac{5 + 4.472}{3} = \dfrac{9.472}{3} \approx 3.157$

The greatest integer less than $y(\sqrt{5})$ is $3$.

Answer: $3$

36017.text:
Consider the matrix $f\left(x\right) = \left[\begin{cases}cosx & - sinx & 0 \\ sinx & cosx & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$. Given below are two statements :
Statement I:$f ( - x )$ is the inverse of the matrix $f ( x )$.
Statement II: $f ( x ) f ( y ) = f ( x + y )$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
36017.sol:
Given: $f\left(x\right) = \left[\begin{cases}cosx & - sinx & 0 \\ sinx & cosx & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ f\left(- x\right) = \left[\begin{cases}cosx & sinx & 0 \\ - sinx & cosx & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) \times f\left(- x\right) = \left[\begin{cases}cosx & - sinx & 0 \\ sinx & cosx & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}cosx & sinx & 0 \\ - sinx & cosx & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) \times f\left(- x\right) = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) \times f\left(- x\right) = I$

$⇒ f\left(- x\right) = {f}^{- 1}\left(x\right)$

Hence statement-I is correct

Now, checking statement II

$⇒ f\left(y\right) = \left[\begin{cases}cosy & - siny & 0 \\ siny & cosy & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ f\left(x\right)f\left(y\right) = \left[\begin{cases}cosx & - sinx & 0 \\ sinx & cosx & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}cosy & - siny & 0 \\ siny & cosy & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ f\left(x\right)f\left(y\right) = \left[\begin{cases}cosxcosy - sinxsiny & - cosxsiny - sinxcosy & 0 \\ sinxcosy + cosxsiny & - sinxsiny + cosxcosy & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ f\left(x\right)f\left(y\right) = \left[\begin{cases}cos ( x + y ) & - sin ( x + y ) & 0 \\ sin ( x + y ) & cos ( x + y ) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ f ( x ) \cdot f ( y ) = f ( x + y )$

Hence statement-II is also correct.

38355.subject: Mathematics
38355.text: If sum of all the solutions of the equation $8cosx \cdot \left(cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6} + x\right) \cdot cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6} - x\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 1$ in $\left[0, \pi\right]$ is $k\pi$, then $k$ is equal to:
38355.sol:
Given equation $8cosx . \left(cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6} + x\right) . cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6} - x\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 1$

We would use the formula

$cos\left(A + B\right) . cos\left(A - B\right) = \cos^{2}A - \sin^{2}B$

Now, $cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6} + x\right) . cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6} - x\right) = \cos^{2}\dfrac{\pi}{6} - \sin^{2}x$

$= \dfrac{3}{4} - \sin^{2}x$

$⇒ 8cosx\left(\dfrac{3}{4} - \sin^{2}x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 1$

$⇒ 8cosx\left(\dfrac{1}{4} - \sin^{2}x\right) = 1$

$⇒ 8cosx\left(\dfrac{1}{4} - \left(1 - \cos^{2}x\right)\right) = 1$

$⇒ 8cosx\left(\cos^{2}x - \dfrac{3}{4}\right) = 1$

$⇒ 8\cos^{3}x - 6cosx = 1$

$⇒ 2\left(4\cos^{3}x - 3cosx\right) = 1$

$⇒ 2cos3x = 1$

$⇒ cos3x = \dfrac{1}{2}$

General Solution $3x = 2n\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{2n\pi}{3} \pm \dfrac{\pi}{9}$

$x \in \left[0, \pi\right]$

$∴ x = \dfrac{\pi}{9}, \dfrac{2\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{9}, \dfrac{2\pi}{3} + \dfrac{\pi}{9}$

$Sum = \dfrac{13\pi}{9}, k = \dfrac{13}{9}$

38945.sol:

The variation of the acceleration due to gravity with height $h$ is given by,

Since the weight at given height is $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of the weight at the surface

$⇒ {g}^{'} = \dfrac{g}{3} ⇒ \dfrac{g}{{\left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{g}{3} ⇒ \left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right) = \sqrt{3} ⇒ h = R\left(\sqrt{3} - 1\right) = 6400 \times \left(1 . 732 - 1\right) = 4685km$

44681.sol:
From conservation of linear momentum,

$mv = \left(4m + m\right){v}_{f}$
${v}_{f} = \dfrac{v}{5}$
From conservation of mechanical energy,
$\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(4m + m\right){v}_{f}^{2} + mgh$
${v}^{2} = 5{v}_{f}^{2} + 2gh$
${v}^{2} = 5 \times {\left(\dfrac{v}{5}\right)}^{2} + 2gh$
$h = \dfrac{2{v}^{2}}{5g}$

47252.text:
Given below are two statements.
Statement-I: Restriction enzyme BamHI has its recognition site in $R^{tet}$ region of pBR322.
Statement-II: E.coli having pBR322 with a desired DNA if inserted at BamHI site can grow in medium containing tetracycline.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true, but Statement II is false
Statement I is false, but Statement II is true
47252.sol:
In the plasmid pBR322, the tetracycline resistance gene (tet^{R}$) contains recognition sites for the restriction enzymes BamHI and SalI. Therefore, Statement-I is true.

When a desired DNA fragment is inserted at the BamHI site, the tetracycline resistance gene gets disrupted due to insertional inactivation. As a result, the recombinant plasmid loses its resistance to tetracycline. Thus, E. coli host cells containing this recombinant pBR322 will not be able to grow in a medium containing tetracycline. Therefore, Statement-II is false.

Answer: Statement I is true, but Statement II is false$

Therefore, from the quantum number values, electron $P$ belongs to $3 d-$ orbital and electron $Q$ to $3 s$ - orbital. Energy of the orbital is $s < p < d < f$.
Hence, energy of electron $P$ is higher than electron $Q$.

52486.text:
A coffee maker makes coffee by passing steam through a mixture of coffee powder, milk and water. If the steam is mixed at the rate of $50g$ per minute in a mug containing $500g$ of mixture, then it takes about ${t}_{0}$ seconds to make coffee at $70 ° C$ when the initial temperature of the mixture is $25 ° C$. Let $m$ gram of steam is condensed in the process of heating mixture from $25 ° C$ to $70 ° C$

Then,
Heat lost by steam = Heat gained by mixture

$⇒$ Heat of condensation of steam + Heat given by water formed = Heat gained by mixture

$⇒ m \cdot L + m{s}_{w}\Delta T = M \cdot {s}_{n}\Delta T$

~

$= 500 \times {s}_{w} \times ( 70 - 25 )$

~

$⇒ m = \dfrac{500 \times {s}_{w} \times 45}{L + 30{s}_{w}}$

~

$⇒ m = 500 \times 45 $\$left(\dfrac{L}{sw} +$30\right)$

~

$⇒ m = $\dfrac{500 \times 45}{( 540 + 30 )} \approx$40g$

Now, in $1min, 50g$ of steam is condensed.

$∴ 40g$ of steam will be condensed in time

~

${t}_{0}$

~

${t}_{0} = $\dfrac{40 \times 60}{50}$s = 48s$

Nearest answer is $45s$.

54385.text: For a given density of a planet, the orbital speed of satellite near the surface of the planet of radius $R$ is proportional to
54385.sol:
Applying Newton's second law to a circular orbit, we have
$\frac{m v^2}{r}=\frac{4 \pi^2 r m}{T^2}=\frac{G M m}{r^2}$
where, $m$ is the mass of satellite, and $v$ is the orbital speed
$T$ is the time period
$\therefore \quad T=\frac{2 \pi r^{3 / 2}}{\sqrt{G M}}$
For $r \approx R$
and $M=\frac{4}{3} \pi R^3 \rho(\rho=$ density of planet $)T=\sqrt{\frac{3 \pi}{\rho G}}$
i.e. $T$ is independent of $R$

56046.subject: Chemistry
56046.text: Rate law for the reaction $\mathrm{aA}+\mathrm{bB} \rightarrow \mathrm{cC}+\mathrm{dD}$ is $\mathrm{r}=\mathrm{k}[\mathrm{A}][\mathrm{B}]$. Which from following conditions does NOT affect the rate of reaction?
options: Concentration of $A$ is doubled and concentration of $B$ is kept constant.
Concentration of $B$ is doubled and concentration of $A$ is kept constant.
Concentration of $B$ is doubled and concentration of $A$ is halved.
Concentration of $A$ is kept constant and concentration of $B$ is halved.
56046.sol:
The rate law for the reaction $\mathrm{aA} + \mathrm{bB} \rightarrow \mathrm{cC} + \mathrm{dD}$ is given as $r = k[\mathrm{A}][\mathrm{B}]$.
With initial concentrations $[\mathrm{A}]_0$ and $[\mathrm{B}]_0$, the initial rate is $r_0 = k[\mathrm{A}]_0[\mathrm{B}]_0$.

Analyzing each condition:

Option A: Doubling $[\mathrm{A}]$ while keeping $[\mathrm{B}]$ constant yields $r_A = k(2[\mathrm{A}]_0)([\mathrm{B}]_0) = 2r_0$, changing the rate.

Option B: Doubling $[\mathrm{B}]$ while keeping $[\mathrm{A}]$ constant gives $r_B = k([\mathrm{A}]_0)(2[\mathrm{B}]_0) = 2r_0$, altering the rate.

Option C: Halving $[\mathrm{A}]$ while doubling $[\mathrm{B}]$ results in $r_C = k(\frac{1}{2}[\mathrm{A}]_0)(2[\mathrm{B}]_0) = r_0$, leaving the rate unchanged.

Option D: Halving $[\mathrm{B}]$ while keeping $[\mathrm{A}]$ constant produces $r_D = k([\mathrm{A}]_0)(\frac{1}{2}[\mathrm{B}]_0) = \frac{1}{2}r_0$, reducing the rate.

Only option C maintains the initial rate, making it the correct choice.

56636.text: Which of the following elements in +3 oxidation state forms colourless compounds?
56636.sol:
The atomic number of $\text{Sc}$ is $21$.

The electronic configuration of $\text{Sc}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{1} 4s^{2}$.

In the $+3$ oxidation state, the electronic configuration of $\text{Sc}^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{0} 4s^{0}$.

Since there are no unpaired electrons in the $d$-orbital of $\text{Sc}^{3+}$, $d-d$ transitions are not possible.

Therefore, $\text{Sc}^{3+}$ forms colourless compounds.

Answer: $\text{Sc}$

57597.subject: Chemistry
57597.text: Which of the following is a fittig reaction?
57597.sol:
The Fittig reaction couples two aryl halides with sodium in dry ether to form a biaryl compound:

$2 \text{Ar-X} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{Ar-Ar} + 2\text{NaX}$

Option A: $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{Br}+\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{Br}+2 \mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{CH}_3+2 \mathrm{NaBr}$ involves an aryl halide and an alkyl halide, characteristic of the Wurtz–Fittig reaction.

Option B: $2 \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{Br}+2 \mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5+2 \mathrm{NaBr}$ uses only alkyl halides, indicating the Wurtz reaction.

Option C: $2 \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{Br}+2 \mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_3+2 \mathrm{NaBr}$ also uses alkyl halides and is another Wurtz reaction.

Option D: $2 \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{Br}+2 \mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5+2 \mathrm{NaBr}$ couples two aryl halides to form biphenyl, matching the definition of the Fittig reaction.

The Fittig reaction is represented by option D.

58791.text: Which of the following defects is observed in steel?

Steel is an alloy composed primarily of iron and a small amount of carbon.

In the crystal lattice of iron, the much smaller carbon atoms occupy the interstitial voids between the iron atoms.

When foreign atoms occupy the interstitial sites of a host lattice, the defect is known as an interstitial impurity defect.

Therefore, steel exhibits an interstitial impurity defect.

Answer: Interstitial impurity defect

59543.text: $V_0$ and $V_t$ are volumes of an ideal gas at $0\ ^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$ and $t\ ^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$ respectively, find ratio $\dfrac{V_t}{V_0}$
59543.sol:
According to Charles's law, at constant pressure, the volume of a fixed mass of an ideal gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature.

$V \propto T$

$\dfrac{V_t}{V_0} = \dfrac{T_t}{T_0}$

The absolute temperatures are $T_0 = 273\text{ K}$ and $T_t = (273 + t)\text{ K}$.

$\dfrac{V_t}{V_0} = \dfrac{273 + t}{273}$

$\dfrac{V_t}{V_0} = 1 + \dfrac{t}{273}$

Answer: $1 + \dfrac{t}{273}$

59967.subject: Chemistry
59967.text: Which among the following pair of properties are intensive?
59967.sol:
The correct answer is (1) surface tension and viscosity.
Intensive properties are properties that do not depend on the amount or size of the substance, and remain the same regardless of the quantity of the material present. On the other hand, extensive properties depend on the amount of substance.
- Surface tension and viscosity are both intensive properties because they are independent of the amount of substance. Surface tension measures the cohesive force at the surface of a liquid, while viscosity measures the resistance of a liquid to flow. Both are properties that remain constant regardless of the amount of liquid.

60272.subject: Mathematics
60272.text: A wire of length 8 units is cut into two parts which are bent respectively in the form of a square and a circle. The least value of the sum of the areas so formed is
60272.sol:
Minimizing the sum of areas formed by bending a wire of length $L = 8$ into a square and circle.

Let $x$ be the length used for the square, so the circle uses $8 - x$. The square's perimeter is $x$, giving side length $s = \frac{x}{4}$ and area $A_s = \frac{x^2}{16}$. The circle's circumference is $8 - x$, so its radius is $r = \frac{8-x}{2\pi}$ and area $A_c = \frac{(8-x)^2}{4\pi}$.

The total area function is $A(x) = \frac{x^2}{16} + \frac{(8-x)^2}{4\pi}$.

Differentiating to find the minimum:
$\frac{dA}{dx} = \frac{x}{8} - \frac{8-x}{2\pi}$

Setting the derivative to zero:
$\frac{x}{8} = \frac{8-x}{2\pi}$
$2\pi x = 64 - 8x$
$x(2\pi + 8) = 64$
$x = \frac{32}{\pi + 4}$

The second derivative $\frac{d^2A}{dx^2} = \frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{2\pi} > 0$ confirms this is a minimum.

The corresponding circle length is $8 - x = \frac{8\pi}{\pi + 4}$. Substituting into the area function:

$A_s = \frac{64}{(\pi + 4)^2}$, $A_c = \frac{16\pi}{(\pi + 4)^2}$

$A_\min = A_s + A_c = \frac{64 + 16\pi}{(\pi + 4)^2} = \frac{16}{\pi + 4}$

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

60566.subject: Mathematics
60566.text: The area of the region common to the parabolas $4y^2 = 9x$ and $3x^2 = 16y$ is...
60566.sol:
The given equations of the parabolas are $4y^2 = 9x$ and $3x^2 = 16y$.

From the second equation, we have $y = \dfrac{3x^2}{16}$. Substituting this into the first equation:

$4\left(\dfrac{3x^2}{16}\right)^2 = 9x$

$\dfrac{9x^4}{64} = 9x$

$x^4 - 64x = 0$

$x(x^3 - 64) = 0$

The real roots are $x = 0$ and $x = 4$.

The required area $A$ is the integral of the upper curve minus the lower curve from $x = 0$ to $x = 4$:

$A = \int_{0}^{4} \left( \dfrac{3}{2}\sqrt{x} - \dfrac{3x^2}{16} \right) dx$

$A = \left[ x^{3/2} - \dfrac{x^3}{16} \right]_{0}^{4}$

$A = \left( 4^{3/2} - \dfrac{4^3}{16} \right) - 0$

$A = 8 - 4 = 4$ sq. units.

Answer: 4 sq. units

60847.subject: Mathematics
60847.text: If $\frac{z-1}{2 z+1} is an imaginary number and if it represents a circle then its radius is$
60847.sol:
Given $z = x + iy$ where $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$, the condition that $\frac{z-1}{2z+1}$ is purely imaginary implies its real part vanishes. Substituting $z = x + iy$ yields:

$\frac{(x-1) + iy}{(2x+1) + 2iy}$

Rationalizing the denominator by multiplying numerator and denominator by the complex conjugate $(2x+1) - 2iy$:

$\frac{[(x-1) + iy][(2x+1) - 2iy]}{(2x+1)^2 + 4y^2}$

Expanding the numerator:

$[(x-1)(2x+1) + 2y^2] + i[3y] = (2x^2 + 2y^2 - x - 1) + i(3y)$

Consequently:

$\frac{z-1}{2z+1} = \frac{2x^2 + 2y^2 - x - 1}{(2x+1)^2 + 4y^2} + i\cdot\frac{3y}{(2x+1)^2 + 4y^2}$

Setting the real part to zero gives $2x^2 + 2y^2 - x - 1 = 0$, which simplifies to:

$x^2 + y^2 - \frac{1}{2}x - \frac{1}{2} = 0$

Comparing with the standard circle equation $x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$ yields $g = -\frac{1}{4}$, $f = 0$, $c = -\frac{1}{2}$. The radius is:

$r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{16} + \frac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{16}} = \frac{3}{4}$

Answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

61287.subject: Mathematics
61287.text: The integrating factor of the differential equation $(1 + t^2) + \left(x - e^{\tan^{-1}t}\right)\dfrac{dt}{dx} = 0$ is
61287.sol:
The given differential equation is $(1 + t^2) + \left(x - e^{\tan^{-1}t}\right)\dfrac{dt}{dx} = 0$

Rearranging the terms, we get:

$(1 + t^2)\dfrac{dx}{dt} + x - e^{\tan^{-1}t} = 0$

$\dfrac{dx}{dt} + \dfrac{1}{1 + t^2}x = \dfrac{e^{\tan^{-1}t}}{1 + t^2}$

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dx}{dt} + Px = Q$, where $P = \dfrac{1}{1 + t^2}$ and $Q = \dfrac{e^{\tan^{-1}t}}{1 + t^2}$

The integrating factor is given by $e^{\int P dt}$

$IF = e^{\int \dfrac{1}{1 + t^2} dt} = e^{\tan^{-1}t}$

Answer: $e^{\tan^{-1}t}$

61337.text: The general solution of the differential equation. $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d} x}+\sin \left(\frac{x+\mathrm{y}}{2}\right)=\sin \left(\frac{x-\mathrm{y}}{2}\right)$ is
options: $\log \tan \left(\frac{y}{2}\right)=c-2 \sin \frac{x}{2}$, where $c$ is the constant of integration
$\log \tan \left(\frac{\mathrm{y}}{4}\right)=\mathrm{c}-2 \sin \left(\frac{x}{2}\right)$, where c is the constant of integration
$\log \left[\tan \left(\frac{\mathrm{y}}{2}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right]=\mathrm{c}-2 \sin x$, where c is the constant of integration
$\log \left[\tan \left(\frac{\mathrm{y}}{4}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right]=\mathrm{c}-2 \sin \frac{x}{2}$, where c is the constant of integration
61337.sol:
The differential equation is $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} + \sin\left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right) = \sin\left(\frac{x-y}{2}\right)$.

Rearranging terms gives $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \sin\left(\frac{x-y}{2}\right) - \sin\left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right)$.

Applying the sum-to-product identity $\sin A - \sin B = 2 \cos\left(\frac{A+B}{2}\right) \sin\left(\frac{A-B}{2}\right)$ with $A = \frac{x-y}{2}$ and $B = \frac{x+y}{2}$ yields $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = -2 \cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right) \sin\left(\frac{y}{2}\right)$.

Separating variables results in $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\sin\left(\frac{y}{2}\right)} = -2 \cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right) \mathrm{d}x$.

Integrating both sides:

$\int \csc\left(\frac{y}{2}\right) \mathrm{d}y = -2 \int \cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right) \mathrm{d}x$

The left side integrates to $2 \log\left|\tan\left(\frac{y}{4}\right)\right|$ and the right side to $-4 \sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)$, giving $2 \log\left|\tan\left(\frac{y}{4}\right)\right| = -4 \sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right) + C'$.

Simplifying yields $\log\left|\tan\left(\frac{y}{4}\right)\right| = c - 2 \sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)$ where $c$ is an integration constant.

This matches option B.

62157.subject: Mathematics
62157.text: The value of integral $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}\,[\log(x^2 + 1) - 2\log x]}{x^4}\,dx$ is equal to...
62157.sol:
Let the given integral be $I = \int \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2+1} [\log(x^2+1) - 2\log x]}{x^4} dx$

$I = \int \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2(1+\dfrac{1}{x^2})}}{x^4} [\log(x^2+1) - \log x^2] dx$

$I = \int \dfrac{x\sqrt{1+\dfrac{1}{x^2}}}{x^4} \log\left(\dfrac{x^2+1}{x^2}\right) dx$

$I = \int \dfrac{1}{x^3}\sqrt{1+\dfrac{1}{x^2}} \log\left(1+\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right) dx$

Substituting $1+\dfrac{1}{x^2} = t$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get $-\dfrac{2}{x^3} dx = dt \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{x^3} dx = -\dfrac{1}{2} dt$

$I = \int \sqrt{t} \log t \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) dt$

$I = -\dfrac{1}{2} \int t^{1/2} \log t dt$

Using integration by parts, taking $\log t$ as the first function and $t^{1/2}$ as the second function:

$I = -\dfrac{1}{2} \left[ \log t \int t^{1/2} dt - \int \left( \dfrac{d}{dt}(\log t) \int t^{1/2} dt \right) dt \right]$

$I = -\dfrac{1}{2} \left[ \log t \left(\dfrac{t^{3/2}}{3/2}\right) - \int \dfrac{1}{t} \left(\dfrac{t^{3/2}}{3/2}\right) dt \right]$

$I = -\dfrac{1}{2} \left[ \dfrac{2}{3} t^{3/2} \log t - \dfrac{2}{3} \int t^{1/2} dt \right]$

$I = -\dfrac{1}{2} \left[ \dfrac{2}{3} t^{3/2} \log t - \dfrac{2}{3} \left(\dfrac{t^{3/2}}{3/2}\right) \right] + c$

$I = -\dfrac{1}{2} \left[ \dfrac{2}{3} t^{3/2} \log t - \dfrac{4}{9} t^{3/2} \right] + c$

$I = t^{3/2} \left[ -\dfrac{1}{3} \log t + \dfrac{2}{9} \right] + c$

Substituting $t = 1+\dfrac{1}{x^2}$ back into the expression:

$I = \left(1+\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right)^{3/2} \left[ -\dfrac{1}{3} \log\left(1+\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right) + \dfrac{2}{9} \right] + c$

63182.sol:
Given a non-singular matrix $A$ satisfying $(A-3I)(A-5I)=0$, expand the product:

$(A-3I)(A-5I)=A^2-8A+15I=0$.

Since $A$ is invertible, multiply both sides by $A^{-1}$:

$A^{-1}(A^2-8A+15I)=A-8I+15A^{-1}=0$.

Rearranging gives $15A^{-1}=8I-A$.

Dividing both sides by 8 yields:

$\frac{15}{8}A^{-1}=I-\frac{1}{8}A$.

This matches option C.

64839.subject: Mathematics
64839.text: The number of values of $x$ in the interval $[0,3 \pi]$ satisfying the equation $2 \sin ^2 x+5 \sin x-3=0$ is
64839.sol:
Solving $2\sin^2x + 5\sin x - 3 = 0$

The equation is quadratic in $\sin x$. Substitute $y = \sin x$, yielding $2y^2 + 5y - 3 = 0$.

Factoring gives $(2y - 1)(y + 3) = 0$. Solutions are $y = \frac{1}{2}$ and $y = -3$.

Since the range of sine is $[-1,1]$, $\sin x = -3$ has no solution.

For $\sin x = \frac{1}{2}$, the general solution is $x = n\pi + (-1)^n\frac{\pi}{6}$, where $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

Within $[0, 3\pi]$, valid values occur for $n = 0, 1, 2, 3$, giving $x = \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{5\pi}{6}, \frac{13\pi}{6}, \frac{17\pi}{6}$.

Thus, there are exactly four solutions.

$\boxed{4}$

67410.text: According to the kinetic theory of gases, when two molecules of a gas collide with each other then
options: both kinetic energy and momentum are conserved.
neither kinetic energy nor momentum is conserved.
momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is not conserved.
kinetic energy is conserved but momentum is not conserved.
67410.sol:

Answer: $\boxed{A}$

69697.text: A black body is at temperature of 5780 K. The energy of radiation emitted by the body at wavelength 300 nm is $U_1$, at wavelength 500 nm is $U_2$ and that at 900 nm is $U_3$ respectively. Wien's constant $b = 2.89 \times 10^6\ \text{nmK}$. This shows that

Using Wien's displacement law, $\lambda_m T = b$.

Substituting the given values:

$\lambda_m = \dfrac{2.89 \times 10^6}{5780} = 500 \text{ nm}$

The maximum energy of radiation is emitted at $\lambda_m = 500 \text{ nm}$.

Since $U_2$ corresponds to the energy at $500 \text{ nm}$, it is the maximum energy.

Therefore, $U_2 > U_1$ and $U_2 > U_3$.

This gives $U_1 < U_2 > U_3$.

Answer: $U_1 < U_2 > U_3$

70127.subject: Physics
70127.text: In a biprism experiment, the distance between $4^{th}$ and $13^{th}$ bright band on the same side is '$y$' when light of wavelength $6000$ Å is used. For a light of wavelength '$\lambda$' the distance between $6^{th}$ and $16^{th}$ bright band on the same side is again '$y$'. The value of '$\lambda$' in Å units is
70127.sol:
The distance of the $n^{th}$ bright band from the central maximum is given by $x_n = n \dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$

The distance between the $4^{th}$ and $13^{th}$ bright band is $y = (13 - 4) \dfrac{\lambda_1 D}{d} = 9 \dfrac{\lambda_1 D}{d}$

The distance between the $6^{th}$ and $16^{th}$ bright band is $y = (16 - 6) \dfrac{\lambda D}{d} = 10 \dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$

Equating the two expressions for $y$:

$9 \dfrac{\lambda_1 D}{d} = 10 \dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$

$9 \lambda_1 = 10 \lambda$

Substituting $\lambda_1 = 6000$:

$9 \times 6000 = 10 \lambda$

$\lambda = \dfrac{54000}{10} = 5400$

Answer: $5400$

70989.text:
Match the parts of respiratory system given in column I with their respective functions in column II and choose the correct option given below.
Column IColumn II
A. Mesethmoid cartilageI. separates thoracic and abdominal cavities
B. 'C' shaped incomplete cartilaginous ringsII. divides nasal cavity into right and left chambers

D. DiaphragmIV. prevents collapsing of trachea
70989.sol:
Mesethmoid cartilage forms the nasal septum, which divides the nasal cavity into right and left chambers. Thus, A matches with II.

'C' shaped incomplete cartilaginous rings are present in the trachea to prevent it from collapsing during inspiration. Thus, B matches with IV.

Epiglottis is a cartilaginous flap that covers the glottis and prevents the entry of food into the trachea during swallowing. Thus, C matches with III.

Diaphragm is a dome-shaped muscular structure that separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominal cavity. Thus, D matches with I.

The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I.

Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

71490.text: In an ovule, one of the male gamete fuses with haploid female gamete to produce a diploid zygote, the process is called
71490.sol:
The fusion of one male gamete with a haploid female gamete (egg cell) to produce a diploid zygote is known as syngamy.

Chalazogamy refers to the entry of the pollen tube into the ovule through the chalazal end.

Mesogamy refers to the entry of the pollen tube through the integuments or funiculus.

Siphonogamy is the condition where male gametes are carried to the female gamete by a pollen tube.

Answer: syngamy

71584.subject: Biology
71584.text: The process by which water from the interface of cell wall and plasma membrane enters into the cytoplasm of root hair cell is ___________.
71584.sol:
Water from the soil first enters the cell wall of the root hair by imbibition and diffusion, as the cell wall is freely permeable.

From the interface of the cell wall and the plasma membrane, water must cross the selectively permeable plasma membrane to enter the cytoplasm.

The movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential is called osmosis.

Therefore, water enters the cytoplasm of the root hair cell through osmosis.

Answer: osmosis

75186.subject: General Ability
75186.text: With which of the following was the Bretton Woods System NOT associated
options: Economic recovery after the Second World War
International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
Establishment of a monetary system based on floating exchange rate
75186.sol:
The Bretton Woods System was established in 1944 to rebuild the international economic system after the Second World War.

It led to the creation of two major international institutions: the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD, now part of the World Bank).

The system was based on fixed exchange rates, where currencies were pegged to the US dollar, which was in turn pegged to gold. It did not establish a monetary system based on floating exchange rates.

Therefore, the establishment of a monetary system based on floating exchange rates is not associated with the Bretton Woods System.

Answer: Establishment of a monetary system based on floating exchange rate

Question: What is $\mathrm{V}+\mathrm{W}$ equal to?
76577.sol:
We have, $(8+3 \sqrt{7})^{20}=\mathrm{U}+\mathrm{V}$....(i)
and $(8-3 \sqrt{7})^{20}=\mathrm{W}$....(ii)
Here, $\mathrm{o} < \mathrm{W} < 1$

& \mathrm{U}+\mathrm{V}+\mathrm{W}=(8+3 \sqrt{7})^{20}+(8-3 \sqrt{7})^{20} \\
& =2\left[{ }^{20} \mathrm{C}_0 \cdot 8^{20}+{ }^{20} \mathrm{C}_2 8^{18} \cdot(3 \sqrt{7})^2+\ldots .+(3 \sqrt{7})^{20}\right]
\end{aligned}$
R.H.S. is an even number.
Also, $\mathrm{o} < \mathrm{V} < 1, \mathrm{o} < \mathrm{W} < 1$ and U is an integer
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{V}+\mathrm{W}$ is an integer $\Rightarrow \mathrm{V}+\mathrm{W}=1$

77321.subject: Mathematics
77321.text: If $2f(x)+f(1-x)=x$, then what is $f(x)$ equal to ?
77321.sol:
Given equation is $2f(x) + f(1-x) = x$.

Replacing $x$ with $1-x$, we get:

$2f(1-x) + f(x) = 1-x$

Multiplying the first equation by $2$, we get:

$4f(x) + 2f(1-x) = 2x$

Subtracting the second equation from this, we get:

$3f(x) = 2x - (1-x)$

$3f(x) = 3x - 1$

$f(x) = x - \dfrac{1}{3}$

Answer: $x- \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

78009.subject: Mathematics
78009.text: An integer is chosen at random from the first 50 integers. What is the probability that the integer is neither divisible by 5 nor 9?
78009.sol:
Total number of integers in the sample space, $n(S) = 50$.

Let $A$ be the event that the chosen integer is divisible by $5$, and $B$ be the event that it is divisible by $9$.

The number of integers divisible by $5$ is $n(A) = 10$.

The number of integers divisible by $9$ is $n(B) = 5$.

The number of integers divisible by both $5$ and $9$ (i.e., divisible by $45$) is $n(A \cap B) = 1$.

The number of integers divisible by either $5$ or $9$ is given by:

$n(A \cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A \cap B) = 10 + 5 - 1 = 14$

The number of integers neither divisible by $5$ nor $9$ is:

$n(A' \cap B') = n(S) - n(A \cup B) = 50 - 14 = 36$

The required probability is:

$P(A' \cap B') = \dfrac{36}{50} = \dfrac{18}{25}$

Answer: $18/25$

78944.subject: Mathematics
78944.text: If $\cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{3}$, then what is the value of $\sin\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{3\theta}{2}\right)$ ?
78944.sol:
Using the trigonometric identity $2\sin A \sin B = \cos(A-B) - \cos(A+B)$, we have:

$\sin\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{3\theta}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\cos\left(\dfrac{3\theta}{2} - \dfrac{\theta}{2}\right) - \cos\left(\dfrac{3\theta}{2} + \dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\right]$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}[\cos\theta - \cos(2\theta)]$

Using the double angle formula $\cos(2\theta) = 2\cos^2\theta - 1$, we get:

$\cos(2\theta) = 2\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^2 - 1 = \dfrac{2}{9} - 1 = -\dfrac{7}{9}$

Substituting the values of $\cos\theta$ and $\cos(2\theta)$:

$\sin\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{3\theta}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{1}{3} - \left(-\dfrac{7}{9}\right)\right]$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{3}{9} + \dfrac{7}{9}\right]$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{10}{9}\right] = \dfrac{5}{9}$

Answer: $\dfrac{5}{9}$

79516.subject: Botany
79516.text: Which one of the following phyla is correctly matched with its two general characteristics?
options:
Chordata
- Body divided into head, thorax and abdomen and respiration by tracheae
- Notochord at some stage and separate anal and urinary openings to the cutside
Echinodermata - Pentamerous radial symmetry and mostly internal fertilization

Mollusca
- Normally oviparous and development through a trochophore or veliger larva
79516.sol:
Arthropoda is the largest phylum of animal kingdom. Body of arthropod is divisible into head, thorax and abdomen. Head and thorax often fused to form cephalothorax. The respiration takes place by general body surface, gills, tracheae or book lungs.
Molluscs are dioecious or monoecious, one or more gonads with gonoducts, opening into renal ducts or to exterior. The fertilization is external or internal, development direct or through free larval forms.
Echinoderms have a pentamerous radial symmetry derived from an original bilateral symmetry. The fertilization is external, development indirect through free-swimming larval forms.
Chordates are sharply distinguished from non-chordates by presence of notochord, dorsal tubular central nervous system and pharyngeal gills slits.

83693.subject: Physics
83693.text: In thermodynamic processes which of the following statements is not true?
options: In an adiabatic process the system is insulated from the surroundings
In an isochoric process pressure remains constant
In an isothermal process the temperature remains constant
83693.sol:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e. In an isochoric process pressure remains constant. CONCEPT: - Thermodynamic process: It is the change in a system from its initial state of thermodynamic equilibrium to the final state of thermodynamic equilibrium. - The various types of thermodynamic processes and their relation with pressure( \((\mathrm{P})\) and volume(V) of gas, is as follows: $
\begin{array}{l} Isobaric process \end{array}\begin{array}{l} - It is a process that takes place under constant pressure. \end{array}
\begin{array}{l} Isochoric process \end{array}$\begin{array}{l} - It is a process where $ the change in volume is zero.
- As the change in volume is zero, the work done is zero. \end{array}$
\begin{array}{l} Isothermal process \end{array}$$\begin{array}{l} - It is a process that takes place under constant temperature. \end{array}$
$\begin{array}{l} Adiabatic process \end{array}$$\begin{array}{l} - It is a process in which no heat is exchanged between the
system and the surrounding i.e. the system is insulated.
- It is represented mathematically as PV= constant \end{array}
EXPLANATION: - An isochoric process is a thermodynamic process that occurs when the change in volume is zero. - Hence the statement 'In an isochoric process pressure remains constant is not true.

85097.subject: Zoology
85097.text: The principle of competitive exclusion was stated by
85097.sol:
Competitive exclusion (By Gause): It states that two closely related species competing for the same resources cannot co-exist indefinitely and the competitively inferior one will be eventually eliminated.

Gause original experiment with ciliates, which is a classic example of this. Paramecium caudatum and Paramecium aurelia, two closely related ciliate protozoans, when grown in separate cultures exhibited typical sigmoid population growth. When both protozoans were placed in the same culture, P. aurelia alone survived after 16 days because it had a more rapid growth rate and thus out-competed P. caudatum for the limited amount of food.

If ${f}_{1}$ and ${f}_{2}$ are the frequencies $( {f}_{1} > {f}_{2} )$ of the two waves, then the beat frequency ${f}_{b} = {f}_{1} - {f}_{2}$

Frequency of ${1}^{st}$ wave,

${f}_{1} = \dfrac{{V}_{1}}{{\lambda}_{1}} = \dfrac{303}{100} \times {10}^{2} = 3.03 \times {10}^{2}Hz$

For ${2}^{nd}$ wave, ${f}_{2} = \dfrac{{V}_{1}}{{\lambda}_{2}} = \dfrac{303}{101} \times {10}^{2} = 3 \times {10}^{2}Hz$

So, beat frequency $= {f}_{1} - {f}_{2}$

$= 3.03 \times {10}^{2} - 3 \times {10}^{2} =. 03 \times {10}^{2} = 3Hz$

96579.subject: Botany
96579.sol:
The movement and exchange of organic and inorganic matter between living and non-living component in a cyclical manner refers to nutrient cycle. These are also called as biogeochemical cycles as there is involvement of biotic and abiotic factors and chemical reactions. There are many important cycles which help in maintaining the biosphere like carbon cycle, nitrogen cycle etc.

Phosphorus is important for the biological membranes and nucleic acids. Also, it is important part of the energy molecule ATP. The natural reservoir of phosphorus is rock and also, phosphorus is released during the breakdown of waste products like guano deposits of birds and bats, and dead organisms by the decomposers like phosphate solubilizing bacteria. These form a part in the phosphorus cycle.

Lithosphere is considered as reservoir for sulfur and phosphorus.

96664.subject: Botany
96664.text: Select the correct statement about productivity from the following.
options: Gross primary productivity is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs.
Secondary productivity depends on the photosynthetic capacity of the plant species inhabiting a particular area.
Productivity is expressed in terms of kg^{–2} yr^{–1} or (kcal m^{–2} )yr^{–1} to compare the productivity of different ecosystems.
Of an approximate NPP of 170 billion tonnes, the productivity of the oceans are only 55 billion tons despite accupying 70% of the earth.
96664.sol:
The rate of biomass production is called productivity. It is expressed in terms of g^{–2} yr^{–1} or (kcal m^{–2})yr^{–1} to compare the productivity of different ecosystems. It can be divided into gross primary productivity (GPP) and net primary productivity (NPP).&
Net primary productivity is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs (herbiviores and decomposers).
Primary productivity depends on the plant species inhabiting a particular area. It also depends on a variety of environmental factors, availability of nutrients and photosynthetic capacity of plants. Therefore, it varies in different types of ecosystems. The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter. Of this, despite occupying about 70 per cent of the surface, the productivity of the oceans are only 55 billion tons.

97479.text:
Consider the following four statements and choose the correct option based on whether they are RIGHT or WRONG.

(I) The sporophyte in liverworts is more elaborate than in mosses.
(II) Salvinia is heterosporous.
(III) The life cycle in all seed-bearing plants is diplontic.
(IV) In Pinus, male and female cones are borne on different trees.
97479.sol:
Salvinia is a genera of Pteridophyte which produces two types of spores - micro and macro. Such type of spores are called heterosporous. The microspore gives rise to male plant and the megaspore forms the female plant.

Liverworts, type of bryophytes, usually grow in moist shady habitats and its plant body is called as thalloid. The sporophyte of liverworts is differentiated into foot, setae and capsule. Mosses are another type of bryophyte whose sporophyte stage has similar three parts like liverworts but more elaborated.

Gymnosperms are heterosporous and the spores are made in sporangia that are borne on sporophylls called stobili or cones. Male cones are the ones bearing the male gametes and female cone bears female gamete. In Pinus, both the cones are found on the same tree unlike in Cycas.

100270.subject: Physics
100270.text:
Match the following columns. \(
Column IColumn II
(A)$\frac{d v}{dt}$(p)Acceleration
(B)$\frac{d |v|}{dt}$(q)Magnitude of acceleration
(C)$\frac{d r}{dt}$(r)Velocity
(D)$\left|\frac{d r}{dt}\right|$(s)Magnitude of velocity
\)
100270.sol:
- Part A: \($\frac{d y}{d t}$\)
- This is the time derivative of velocity. By definition, the rate of change of velocity is acceleration. Since velocity is a vector, its derivative is also a vector, representing acceleration.
- Therefore, (A) matches with (p) Acceleration.
- Part B: \($\frac{d|v|}{d t}$\)
- This is the time derivative of the magnitude of velocity (speed). This quantity is the rate of change of speed. This is NOT the same as the magnitude of acceleration. For example, in uniform circular motion, the speed is constant, so \($\frac{d|v|}{d t}=$0\), but the object is accelerating because its direction is changing. The magnitude of acceleration is nonzero in this case.
- Therefore, (B) matches with (q) Magnitude of acceleration.
- Part C: \($\frac{d r}{d t}$\)
- This is the time derivative of the position vector. By definition, the rate of change of position is velocity.
- Therefore, (C) matches with (r) Velocity.
- Part D: \($\frac{|d r|}{d t}$\)
- The term \($\frac{|d r|}{d t}$\) is the magnitude of the rate of change of the position vector. As we know, \($\frac{d r}{d t}$\) is the velocity, so taking its magnitude gives us the magnitude of velocity or speed.
- Therefore, (D) matches with (s) Magnitude of velocity.

100978.subject: Physics
100978.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
100978.text: A particle of mass $' m '$, moving with a velocity $' v '$ makes an elastic collision in one dimension with a stationary particle of mass $' m '$. During the collision, they remain in contact with each other for an extremely small time $' T '$: Their force of contact, with time is shown in the figure. Then ${F}_{0} =$
100978.sol:
In an elastic head-on collision between two particles, the velocity of the particle gets exchanged, therefore net change of momentum of a particle is, $∆ p = m ∆ v = m\left(v - 0\right) = mv$

From newton's second law, the rate of change of momentum is force.

$F = \dfrac{d p}{d t}$
$⇒ F d t = d p$
$⇒ FT = ∆ p$

Here, $F$is force of contact during the collision for a small-time $T$that causes the $∆ p$change in momentum of particle.

Thus, the area under the graph of $F - t$curve gives the change in momentum.

$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \left(\dfrac{T}{4}\right) \times \left({F}_{0}\right) + \left(\dfrac{3T}{4} - \dfrac{T}{4}\right) \times \left({F}_{0}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2} \times \left(T - \dfrac{3T}{4}\right) \times \left({F}_{0}\right)$
$= \dfrac{3}{4}T{F}_{0}$

Therefore,

$\text{Area} = ∆ p$
$⇒ mv = \dfrac{3}{4}T{F}_{0}$
$⇒ {F}_{0} = \dfrac{4mv}{3T}$

101684.subject: Physics
101684.text:
Match List-I with List-II for a small solid sphere of volume $V$, radius $r$ and density $\rho$ falling through a viscous fluid of density $\sigma$ (where $\rho > \sigma$) and coefficient of viscosity $\eta$.

List-IList-II
(A) Buoyant force(I) $V\sigma g$
(B) Initial acceleration when just released(II) $V(\rho - \sigma)g$
(C) Viscous force at terminal velocity(III) $g\left(1 - \dfrac{\sigma}{\rho}\right)$
(D) Terminal velocity(IV) $\dfrac{2r^2(\rho - \sigma)g}{9\eta}$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
101684.sol:
(A) Buoyant force is the weight of the displaced fluid. For a sphere of volume $V$ in a fluid of density $\sigma$, $F_b = V\sigma g$. This matches (I).

(B) When just released, the initial velocity is zero, so the viscous force is zero. The net downward force is $W - F_b = V\rho g - V\sigma g$.
Initial acceleration $a = \dfrac{\text{Net force}}{\text{Mass}} = \dfrac{V(\rho - \sigma)g}{V\rho} = g\left(1 - \dfrac{\sigma}{\rho}\right)$. This matches (III).

(C) At terminal velocity, the sphere moves with constant velocity, so the net force is zero.
Viscous force $F_v = W - F_b = V\rho g - V\sigma g = V(\rho - \sigma)g$. This matches (II).

(D) The terminal velocity of a sphere of radius $r$ falling in a viscous fluid of coefficient of viscosity $\eta$ is given by Stokes' law as $v_t = \dfrac{2r^2(\rho - \sigma)g}{9\eta}$. This matches (IV).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A) - (I), (B) - (III), (C) - (II), (D) - (IV).

Answer: (A) - (I), (B) - (III), (C) - (II), (D) - (IV)

102442.subject: Physics
102442.text: A simple pendulum has a time period $T_0$ when oscillating in a stationary elevator in air. The pendulum is then suspended from the ceiling of an elevator that is accelerating upwards with an acceleration $g$. The pendulum bob is completely immersed in a non-viscous liquid whose density is half the density of the material of the bob. The new time period of the pendulum will be
102442.sol:
The time period of the pendulum in a stationary elevator in air is:
$T_0 = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}$

When the elevator accelerates upwards with acceleration $a = g$, the apparent acceleration due to gravity in the non-inertial frame of the elevator is:
$g_{app} = g + a = g + g = 2g$

When the bob is immersed in a liquid, the buoyant force acts opposite to the apparent gravity. The effective acceleration due to gravity $g_{eff}$ is given by:
$g_{eff} = g_{app} \left(1 - \dfrac{\rho_L}{\rho_S}\right)$
where $\rho_L$ is the density of the liquid and $\rho_S$ is the density of the bob.

Given $\rho_L = \dfrac{\rho_S}{2}$, we substitute the values:
$g_{eff} = 2g \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 2g \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = g$

The new time period is:
$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g_{eff}}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}} = T_0$

Ignoring the elevator's acceleration would incorrectly yield $\sqrt{2}T_0$, and applying buoyancy to $g$ instead of $g_{app}$ would incorrectly yield $\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}T_0$.

Answer: $T_0$

103350.subject: Physics
103350.text: The variation of terminal voltage ($V$) versus current ($I$) drawn from a cell is plotted as a straight line. The graph intersects the voltage axis at $10\text{ V}$ and the current axis at $5\text{ A}$. If this cell is connected across an external resistor of $3\ \Omega$, what will be the terminal voltage across the cell?
103350.sol:
From the given $V-I$ graph description, the intercept on the voltage axis represents the emf ($E$) of the cell (when $I = 0$).

Thus, $E = 10\text{ V}$

The intercept on the current axis represents the maximum current or short-circuit current ($I_{\max}$) when the terminal voltage is zero.

$I_{\max} = \dfrac{E}{r} = 5\text{ A}$

Internal resistance $r = \dfrac{10}{5} = 2\ \Omega$

When the cell is connected to an external resistor $R = 3\ \Omega$, the current in the circuit is:

$I = \dfrac{E}{R + r} = \dfrac{10}{3 + 2} = \dfrac{10}{5} = 2\text{ A}$

The terminal voltage across the cell is the voltage drop across the external resistor:

$V = IR = 2 \times 3 = 6\text{ V}$

Answer: $6\text{ V}$

103915.subject: Physics
103915.text: A rectangular loop of area $2.5 \text{ m}^2$ lies flat in the x-z plane. A uniform magnetic field is applied in the region, given by $\vec{B} = (0.3 \hat{i} - 0.4 \hat{j} + 1.2 \hat{k}) \text{ T}$. The magnitude of the magnetic flux through the loop is:
103915.sol:
Since the rectangular loop lies in the x-z plane, its area vector is directed along the y-axis (perpendicular to the plane).

Thus, the area vector can be written as $\vec{A} = 2.5 \hat{j} \text{ m}^2$.

The magnetic flux $\Phi$ is the dot product of the magnetic field vector and the area vector:

$\Phi = \vec{B} \cdot \vec{A}$

$\Phi = (0.3 \hat{i} - 0.4 \hat{j} + 1.2 \hat{k}) \cdot (2.5 \hat{j})$

$\Phi = (-0.4) \times 2.5 = -1.0 \text{ Wb}$

The magnitude of the magnetic flux is $1.0 \text{ Wb}$.

Answer: $1.0 \text{ Wb}$

104142.subject: Physics
104142.text:
A series LCR circuit with inductance $L = 0.1\text{ H}$ and capacitance $C = 10\text{ }\mu\text{F}$ is connected across various voltage sources. Match the voltage sources in List-I with the corresponding steady-state behavior of the circuit in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) $V = V_0 \sin(1000t)$(I) Current leads the voltage
(B) $V = V_0 \sin(500t)$(II) Current lags the voltage
(C) $V = V_0 \sin(2000t)$(III) Current is in phase with the voltage
(D) $10\text{ V}$ DC source(IV) Steady state current is zero

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
104142.sol:
The resonant angular frequency of the LCR circuit is:
$\omega_0 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{0.1 \times 10 \times 10^{-6}}} = 1000\text{ rad s}^{-1}$

(A) For $V = V_0 \sin(1000t)$, $\omega = 1000\text{ rad s}^{-1}$. Since $\omega = \omega_0$, the circuit is at resonance and the current is in phase with the voltage. (A) matches with (III).

(B) For $V = V_0 \sin(500t)$, $\omega = 500\text{ rad s}^{-1}$. Since $\omega < \omega_0$, capacitive reactance $X_C$ is greater than inductive reactance $X_L$. The circuit is capacitive, so the current leads the voltage. (B) matches with (I).

(C) For $V = V_0 \sin(2000t)$, $\omega = 2000\text{ rad s}^{-1}$. Since $\omega > \omega_0$, inductive reactance $X_L$ is greater than capacitive reactance $X_C$. The circuit is inductive, so the current lags the voltage. (C) matches with (II).

(D) For a $10\text{ V}$ DC source, $\omega = 0$. The capacitor offers infinite reactance ($X_C = \infty$) and blocks direct current, so the steady state current is zero. (D) matches with (IV).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV)

104199.text: When power is drawn from the secondary coil of the transformer, the dynamic resistance
104199.sol: When the secondary coil circuit is open, the magnetic flux in the core is produced by the primary current only. When the secondary circuit is closed, the currents in the secondary coil also produce magnetic flux in the core but in opposite direction. This decreases the core flux and hence reduces the back emf produced in the primary coil. The source emf is now in excess of the back emf, more current is drawn in the primary coil. Hence, power factor is no longer zero. The power factor has increased or the phase difference is no longer $90^{\circ}$, ie, phase difference has decreased. Thus, dynamic resistance has increased.

104683.subject: Physics
104683.text:
In a Young's double slit experiment, the maximum intensity of light on the screen is $I_0$. Match the path differences given in List-I with their corresponding intensities given in List-II.

List-I (Path Difference)List-II (Intensity)
(A) $\dfrac{\lambda}{6}$(I) $0$
(B) $\dfrac{\lambda}{4}$(II) $\dfrac{I_0}{4}$
(C) $\dfrac{\lambda}{3}$(III) $\dfrac{I_0}{2}$
(D) $\dfrac{\lambda}{2}$(IV) $\dfrac{3I_0}{4}$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
104683.sol:
Phase difference $\phi$ is related to path difference $\Delta x$ by $\phi = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \Delta x$.

The intensity $I$ at a point on the screen is given by $I = I_0 \cos^2\left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)$.

For (A) $\Delta x = \dfrac{\lambda}{6}$, $\phi = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$. $I = I_0 \cos^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = I_0 \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{3I_0}{4}$. This matches (IV).

For (B) $\Delta x = \dfrac{\lambda}{4}$, $\phi = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$. $I = I_0 \cos^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = I_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 = \dfrac{I_0}{2}$. This matches (III).

For (C) $\Delta x = \dfrac{\lambda}{3}$, $\phi = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$. $I = I_0 \cos^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = I_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{I_0}{4}$. This matches (II).

For (D) $\Delta x = \dfrac{\lambda}{2}$, $\phi = \pi$. $I = I_0 \cos^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0$. This matches (I).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

104873.subject: Physics
104873.text: The energy required to ionize an unknown hydrogen-like species from its first excited state is exactly $13.6 \mathrm{eV}$. Identify the species.
104873.sol:
The ionization energy of a hydrogen-like species from a state with principal quantum number $n$ is given by $E = 13.6 \dfrac{Z^2}{n^2} \mathrm{eV}$, where $Z$ is the atomic number.

The first excited state corresponds to $n = 2$.

Given that the ionization energy from this state is $13.6 \mathrm{eV}$, we can write:
$13.6 = 13.6 \times \dfrac{Z^2}{2^2}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{Z^2}{4} = 1$

$\Rightarrow Z^2 = 4$

$\Rightarrow Z = 2$

The species with atomic number $Z = 2$ is the helium ion ($\mathrm{He}^{+}$).

Answer: $\mathrm{He}^{+}$ ion

113517.text: Formula of metal oxide with metal deficiency defect in its crystal is $A_{0.8} \mathrm{O}$. The crystal contains $A^{2+}$ and $A^{3+}$ ions. The fraction of metal existing as $A^{2+}$ ions in the crystal is
113517.sol:
$A: \mathrm{O}=0.8: 1=80: 100$
Thus, if there are $100 \mathrm{O}$ atoms, then number of $A$ atoms $=80$
Charge on $100 \mathrm{O}^{2-}$ ions $=100 \times(-2)=-200$
Suppose number of $A$ atoms present as $A^{2+}=x$
$\therefore \quad$ Number of $\mathrm{A}$ atoms present as $A^{3+}=80-x$
Total charge on $A^{2+}$ and $A^{3+}=x \times(+2)$
$+(80-x) \times(+3)$
$=2 x+240-3 x=240-x$
As metal oxide is neutral,
Total charge on cations $=$ total charge on anions
$\therefore \quad 240-x=200$ or $x=40$
$\therefore \quad$ Fraction of metal existing as $A^{2+}$ ions in the crystal $=40 / 80=0.5$

116344.subject: Chemistry
116344.text: Which of the following pairs of molecules/ions have the same hybridization for their central atom, but different molecular geometries, and consist of one polar and one non-polar species?
116344.sol:
Let us analyze each pair based on VSEPR theory:

$\text{XeF}_4$ and $\text{XeOF}_4$:
In $\text{XeF}_4$, Xe has 4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs ($\text{sp}^3\text{d}^2$ hybridization). Its geometry is square planar, which is highly symmetrical, making it non-polar.
In $\text{XeOF}_4$, Xe has 5 bond pairs (treating the double bond to O as one superpair for geometry) and 1 lone pair ($\text{sp}^3\text{d}^2$ hybridization). Its geometry is square pyramidal, which is asymmetrical, making it polar.
This pair has the same hybridization, different geometries, and one is polar while the other is non-polar.

$\text{XeF}_2$ and $\text{I}_3^-$:
Both have $\text{sp}^3\text{d}$ hybridization, 2 bond pairs, and 3 lone pairs. Both are linear and non-polar. (Fails criteria)

$\text{SF}_4$ and $\text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$:
Both have $\text{sp}^3\text{d}$ hybridization, 4 bond pairs, and 1 lone pair. Both have a see-saw geometry and are polar. (Fails criteria)

$\text{PCl}_5$ and $\text{BrF}_5$:
$\text{PCl}_5$ is $\text{sp}^3\text{d}$ hybridized (trigonal bipyramidal, non-polar). $\text{BrF}_5$ is $\text{sp}^3\text{d}^2$ hybridized (square pyramidal, polar). They have different hybridizations. (Fails criteria)

Answer: $\text{XeF}_4$ and $\text{XeOF}_4$

119273.text:
Consider the following reagents:
(i) Ammonia
(ii) Sodium bisulfite
(iii) Hydrazine
(iv) Hydrogen cyanide
(v) Semicarbazide

How many of the above reagents react with benzaldehyde via a nucleophilic addition-elimination mechanism?
119273.sol:
Benzaldehyde reacts with ammonia derivatives ($\mathrm{NH}_2-\mathrm{Z}$) via a nucleophilic addition-elimination mechanism, resulting in the formation of a $>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{Z}$ bond and the elimination of a water molecule.

Among the given reagents:
(i) Ammonia ($\mathrm{NH}_3$) forms an imine (addition-elimination).
(ii) Sodium bisulfite ($\mathrm{NaHSO}_3$) forms a bisulfite addition product (pure addition).
(iii) Hydrazine ($\mathrm{NH}_2\mathrm{NH}_2$) forms a hydrazone (addition-elimination).
(iv) Hydrogen cyanide ($\mathrm{HCN}$) forms a cyanohydrin (pure addition).
(v) Semicarbazide ($\mathrm{NH}_2\mathrm{NHCONH}_2$) forms a semicarbazone (addition-elimination).

Therefore, exactly three reagents [(i), (iii), and (v)] undergo nucleophilic addition-elimination.

Answer: 3

123649.subject: Botany
123649.text: What is the significance of the process of mitosis in cell repair?
options: Mitosis results in the formation of syncytium.
Mitosis is essential for the cell to divide to restore the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio.
Mitosis contributes to the repair of damaged cells.
Mitosis is only important in the growth of multicellular organisms.
123649.sol: Mitosis usually results in the production of diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complement. Cell growth results in disturbing the ratio between the nucleus and the cytoplasm. It therefore becomes essential for the cell to divide to restore the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio. A very significant contribution of mitosis is cell repair. The cells of the upper layer of the epidermis, cells of the lining of the gut, and blood cells are being constantly replaced. Mitotic divisions in the meristematic tissues – the apical and the lateral cambium, result in a continuous growth of plants throughout their life.

124051.text: How many doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules are present in the axoneme?
124051.sol: The electron microscopic study of a cilium or the flagellum show that they are covered with plasma membrane. Their core called the axoneme, possesses a number of microtubules running parallel to the long axis. The axoneme usually has nine doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules, and a pair of centrally located microtubules. Such an arrangement of axonemal microtubules is referred to as the 9+2 array
